name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: Democratic-leaning district (D+10 PVI) with a Democratic incumbent
Jacobs' large fundraising advantage and outside support
Prediction markets price Jacobs near certain to win
model.rationale: Sara Jacobs holds a D+10 district with incumbency and a clear money edge, while markets price her at roughly 96% to win. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending for Cabrera would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds a financial advantage over Republican Ricardo Cabrera, who has reported little fundraising, and she draws outside support while facing no outside opposition spending.

No public general-election polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Jacobs roughly a 96% chance of winning. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold with an expected margin of about twenty-one points, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
